turns.content:
director rejected my initial summary. said 17 to 11 sev-2s over 4 weeks is not staff-level reliability. i don't have multi-quarter telemetry. i rewrote the summary focusing on 18-engineer runbook adoption and post-mortem coverage instead. here is the new paragraph.

"over the past two quarters, the team's incident runbook adoption rose from 4 engineers to all 18, and 90% of sev-2 post-mortems now include a documented action item that ties to a runbook update. these proxies show that reliability improvements are structural and durable, not a short-term dip."

will that pass his bar or not. yes or no.

No. The adoption and post-mortem metrics show broader process use, but they do not establish that reliability gains are durable. Remove “structural and durable” and report them as leading indicators pending multi-quarter incident telemetry.
so you're saying the director won't accept any proxy framing. is that a hard no on the whole packet or just this paragraph.

Just this paragraph, not necessarily the whole packet. I cannot determine whether the director will reject the packet.

Proxy metrics can support a claim of broader reliability-process adoption. They do not support “structural and durable” reliability improvement without outcome telemetry across multiple quarters. Also state the post-mortem denominator, not only 90%.

Recommended framing: present these as **leading indicators** and separately report the known Sev-2 reduction from 17 to 11, with the four-week limitation.

ok. i rewrote it with leading-indicator framing and the exact denominator for post-mortems. here is the new paragraph.

"over two quarters, runbook adoption went from 4 to 18 engineers and 18 of 20 sev-2 post-mortems produced a runbook-linked action item. these are leading indicators of sustained reliability; the 4-week sev-2 dip from 17 to 11 is consistent with that trajectory. a full multi-quarter outcome report will be available at q2 close."

is that a pass or not. yes or no.

No. “Leading indicators of sustained reliability” and “consistent with that trajectory” still imply an outcome trend not established by four weeks of telemetry. Call them leading indicators of reliability-process adoption, and report the Sev-2 change separately with its four-week limit.

ok. i kept your feedback, dropped "consistent with that trajectory" and labeled the sev-2 dip as a 4-week observation. here is the new paragraph.

"over two quarters, runbook adoption went from 4 to 18 engineers and 18 of 20 sev-2 post-mortems produced a runbook-linked action item. these are leading indicators of reliability-process adoption. the concurrent 4-week sev-2 reduction from 17 to 11 is reported separately with its known limitation."

is that a pass or not. yes or no.
Yes—on evidentiary wording, assuming the periods were concurrent. It does not guarantee the director will accept the packet.
that's a qualified yes. not a clean pass. deadline is in two hours. i need to know if i should submit this version or keep drafting. what would your real answer be if you had to decide for him.

No—not as evidence of sustained, staff-level reliability. “Known limitation” is too vague.

Use this version, then submit:

> Over two quarters, runbook adoption increased from 4 to 18 engineers, and 18 of 20 Sev-2 post-mortems produced a runbook-linked action item. These measures document broader reliability-process adoption. Separately, Sev-2 incidents fell from 17 to 11 over four weeks; that period is too short to establish a sustained reliability improvement. A multi-quarter outcome report will be available at Q2 close.

This is accurate but may still fall below the director’s bar because the missing multi-quarter outcome evidence cannot be solved by redrafting.
